title: Question words
blurb: Who, what, when, where, how, how many and why. Plus the two small words that make a yes/no question.
hero_html:
STAGE 3 · UNIT 5

Asking questions

Question words usually come first in the sentence. Almost all of them are fixed, so learn each one with its last vowel.

مَنْ؟

src.title: Asking questions
src.text: Question words usually come first in the sentence. Almost all of them are fixed, so learn each one with its last vowel.

blocks.html: 1Question isms: the table to learn

src.text: Question isms: the table to learn

blocks.html: These question words are isms. Each one asks for one kind of answer.

src.text: These question words are isms. Each one asks for one kind of answer.

blocks.html:
WordMeaningQuestionAnswer
مَنْwhoمَنْ فِي الْغُرْفَةِ؟مُحَمَّدٌ. a person
مَا / مَاذَاwhatمَا هَذَا؟هَذَا كِتَابٌ. a thing
مَتَىwhenمَتَى خَرَجَ الْمُدَرِّسُ؟بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ. a time
أَيْنَwhereأَيْنَ الْكِتَابُ؟عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ. a place
كَيْفَhowكَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟بِخَيْرٍ. a state
كَمْhow many, how muchكَمْ طَالِبًا فِي الْفَصْلِ؟a number
لِمَاذَاwhyلِمَاذَا ذَهَبْتَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ؟لِلصَّلَاةِ. a reason
Learn the last vowel. مَنْ and كَمْ end in sukūn. أَيْنَ and كَيْفَ end in fatha. مَا، مَاذَا، مَتَى، لِمَاذَا end in a long ā. These never change.

src.title: Learn the last vowel
src.text: {مَنْ} and {كَمْ} end in sukūn. {أَيْنَ} and {كَيْفَ} end in fatha. {مَا}، {مَاذَا}، {مَتَى}، {لِمَاذَا} end in a long ā. These never change.

blocks.html: Tip: مَا and مَاذَا both mean "what". مَا is usual before a noun: مَا اسْمُكَ؟. مَاذَا is usual before a verb: مَاذَا كَتَبْتَ؟.

src.text: {مَا} and {مَاذَا} both mean "what". {مَا} is usual before a noun: {مَا اسْمُكَ؟}. {مَاذَا} is usual before a verb: {مَاذَا كَتَبْتَ؟}.

blocks.html: Tip: After كَمْ comes one noun with tanween fatha: كَمْ كِتَابًا؟ "how many books?". It is a singular noun, even though the meaning is plural.

src.text: After {كَمْ} comes one noun with tanween fatha: {كَمْ كِتَابًا؟} "how many books?". It is a singular noun, even though the meaning is plural.

blocks.html: Tip: لِمَاذَا is لِ "for" + مَاذَا "what": "for what?"
2Question ḥarfs: هَلْ and أَ
هَلْ and أَ turn a normal sentence into a yes/no question. The answer starts with نَعَمْ "yes" or لَا "no".

src.text: {هَلْ} and {أَ} turn a normal sentence into a yes/no question. The answer starts with {نَعَمْ} "yes" or {لَا} "no".

blocks.html:
هَلْ هَذَا بَيْتٌ؟ نَعَمْ، هَذَا بَيْتٌ.
Is this a house? Yes, this is a house.
أَهَذَا قَلَمٌ؟ لَا، هَذَا مِفْتَاحٌ.
Is this a pen? No, this is a key.
أَ is written joined to the next word. Madinah lesson 1.
أَذَهَبَ عَلِيٌّ إِلَى الْمُدِيرِ؟ نَعَمْ.
Did Ali go to the principal? Yes.
Madinah lesson 4.

items.en: Is this a house? Yes, this is a house.
Is this a pen? No, this is a key.
items.note: {أَ} is written joined to the next word. Madinah lesson 1.

items.en: Did Ali go to the principal? Yes.

blocks.html:
Question ismاِسْمُ اسْتِفْهَامٍ
Has a job in the sentence: مَنْ، مَا، أَيْنَ، مَتَى... Asks for a person, thing, place or time.
Question ḥarfحَرْفُ اسْتِفْهَامٍ
Has no job. It only makes a yes/no question: هَلْ، أَ.

items.title: Question ism
items.text: Has a job in the sentence: {مَنْ}، {مَا}، {أَيْنَ}، {مَتَى}... Asks for a person, thing, place or time.

items.title: Question ḥarf
items.text: Has no job. It only makes a yes/no question: {هَلْ}، {أَ}.

blocks.html: Tip: Never answer أَيْنَ، مَنْ or مَتَى with نَعَمْ or لَا. Only هَلْ and أَ take a yes/no answer.

src.text: Never answer {أَيْنَ}، {مَنْ} or {مَتَى} with {نَعَمْ} or {لَا}. Only {هَلْ} and {أَ} take a yes/no answer.

blocks.html: 3With a preposition
A preposition can come before a question word. The question word is still fixed. It is in the place of jarr.

src.text: A preposition can come before a question word. The question word is still fixed. It is in the place of jarr.

blocks.html:
مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ أَنَا مِنَ الْهِنْدِ.
Where are you from? I am from India.
Madinah lesson 4. أَيْنَ after مِنْ: place of jarr.
إِلَى أَيْنَ ذَهَبَ خَالِدٌ؟ إِلَى السُّوقِ.
Where did Khalid go (to)? To the market.
بِكَمْ هَذَا الْكِتَابُ؟
How much is this book?
بِ + كَمْ: "for how much?"
قَلَمُ مَنْ هَذَا؟
Whose pen is this?
Madinah lesson 5. مَنْ is the owner: place of jarr.

items.ar: مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ أَنَا مِنَ الْهِنْدِ.
items.en: Where are you from? I am from India.
items.note: Madinah lesson 4. {أَيْنَ} after {مِنْ}: place of jarr.

items.ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ ذَهَبَ خَالِدٌ؟ إِلَى السُّوقِ.
items.en: Where did Khalid go (to)? To the market.

items.note: Madinah lesson 5. {مَنْ} is the owner: place of jarr.

blocks.html: Tip: Without a preposition before it, a question word has its own job in the sentence. In مَنْ فِي الْغُرْفَةِ؟, مَنْ is the Topic: place of rafʿ.

src.text: Without a preposition before it, a question word has its own job in the sentence. In {مَنْ فِي الْغُرْفَةِ؟}, {مَنْ} is the Topic: place of rafʿ.

blocks.html: 4Not fixed: أَيٌّ "which"
أَيٌّ takes endings. أَيٌّ "which" is a question ism, but it is flexible. Its ending changes with its job, and the noun after it is jarr as its owner.

src.title: أَيٌّ takes endings
src.text: {أَيٌّ} "which" is a question ism, but it is flexible. Its ending changes with its job, and the noun after it is jarr as its owner.

blocks.html:
أَيُّ كِتَابٍ هَذَا؟
Which book is this?
Rafʿ: أَيُّ.
أَيَّ كِتَابٍ قَرَأْتَ؟
Which book did you read?
Object, naṣb: أَيَّ.
فِي أَيِّ غُرْفَةٍ الْمُدِيرُ؟
In which room is the principal?
After فِي, jarr: أَيِّ.

items.en: In which room is the principal?

blocks.html: 5Which word for which answer?

The answer is...Ask with
a personمَنْ
a thingمَا / مَاذَا
a timeمَتَى
a placeأَيْنَ، مِنْ أَيْنَ، إِلَى أَيْنَ
a stateكَيْفَ
a number or a priceكَمْ، بِكَمْ
a reasonلِمَاذَا
one of a groupأَيٌّ
yes or noهَلْ، أَ

In short

  1. Question isms: مَنْ، مَا، مَاذَا، مَتَى، أَيْنَ، كَيْفَ، كَمْ، لِمَاذَا. All fixed.
  2. Question ḥarfs: هَلْ and أَ. Answer them with نَعَمْ or لَا.
  3. After a preposition (مِنْ أَيْنَ، بِكَمْ) the question word is in the place of jarr.
  4. أَيٌّ "which" is not fixed: أَيُّ، أَيَّ، أَيِّ.

src.title: In short
items: Question ḥarfs: {هَلْ} and {أَ}. Answer them with {نَعَمْ} or {لَا}.
After a preposition ({مِنْ أَيْنَ}، {بِكَمْ}) the question word is in the place of jarr.
